annotation.title_clean: Ethical Algorithms in Human-Robot-Interaction. A Proposal
annotation.title_en: Ethical Algorithms in Human-Robot-Interaction. A Proposal
annotation.venue: Computer Science & Information Technology (CS & IT), AIRCC Publishing Corporation
annotation.summary_en: This philosophical conference paper argues that autonomous robots need a human-like ethical competence to be trusted in human-robot interaction. Because robots cannot take a moral stance, the paper proposes a logical model of meta-ethical arguments, based on common goods and moral demands, that could serve as a pattern for programming ethical algorithms into autonomous robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: Trust in autonomous robots depends on reliability, predictability and ethical competence.
Robots cannot adopt the human moral stance, so ethical competence must be implemented through ethical algorithms.
Moral demands protect common goods and are evident, universal and categorical.
Proposes a general logical form of meta-ethical arguments as a template for ethical algorithms.
